subject: Chemistry
title: The Radium Girls Revisited
description: A 60-second lesson on The Radium Girls Revisited.

hook.text: In the 1920s, women painting radium watch dials were told the paint was safe. They pointed their brushes with their lips.

buildup.text: Radium behaves like calcium in the body. Once swallowed, it deposited in bones and irradiated tissue from inside.

discovery.text: Workers developed 'radium jaw'—their jawbones crumbled from radiation necrosis. Teeth fell out. Bones snapped.

twist.text: When five workers sued, the company hired doctors to declare them healthy. One doctor secretly worked for the company.

climax.text: They won their case in 1928. Their lawsuit established that companies are liable for occupational diseases.

punchline.text: Licked brushes, radium in bones, jaws crumbling. Their pain created worker safety law.

quiz.question: Why did radium deposit in the workers' bones?
options: Radium mimics calcium and is absorbed into bone tissue, irradiating from inside
Radium is attracted to the iron in bone marrow
The paint contained a bone-dissolving acid along with radium

details.summary: The Radium Girls were young women who painted luminous watch dials with radium-based paint in the early 1900s and were instructed to shape their brushes with their lips..
details.whyItMatters: The Radium Girls' case established the right of workers to sue employers for occupational hazards and led to safety standards that protect millions of workers from toxic exposure today.
takeaways: Workers were told radium paint was harmless and lip-pointed brushes
Radium accumulated in bones, causing devastating health effects
Their lawsuits established occupational disease liability precedents

faq.question: How did radium cause such devastating effects on the workers?
faq.answer: Radium is chemically similar to calcium, so the body deposits it in bones. Once there, its radioactive decay destroys surrounding bone tissue, causing necrosis, fractures, and bone cancer. The jaw was especially affected because workers ingested radium through lip-tipping their brushes.

faq.question: What legal precedent did the Radium Girls establish?
faq.answer: Their lawsuits established that employers are liable for occupational diseases caused by toxic exposure, not just acute injuries. This precedent enabled the development of occupational safety regulations and the right of workers to seek compensation for chronic chemical exposure diseases.
